proposed_tool_changes.tool: babelfont-rs (follow-up commit on PR #91, branch pr-ff-os2-defaults @119f2be)
proposed_tool_changes.description: In fontforge_standard_height.rs, look a glyph up by ANY of its codepoints, not just the first. Iterate glyphs in order and take the first glyph mapped to the codepoint, whether as its own codepoint or as an alternate (AltUni2). This is what FontForge's SFGetChar -> SFFindGID -> SCUniMatch does: a single pass over gids matching unicodeenc OR any altuni. The code is the same at b69c9652 (20110222), 5a11aa4c (20120906) and master. The change renames glyphs_by_primary_codepoint to glyphs_by_codepoint and adds the unit test test_a_glyph_is_found_by_an_alternate_codepoint.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Harness runs: KottaOne, Macondo and Rosarivo-Italic go from BLOCKING 1 to CLEAN 0 (runs/altuni/). No other gate line changes (runs/nothing_else_opened-before-altuni.txt). The .glyphs change only in x-height: 81->76, 25->24, 229->217. The four CLEAN siblings stay CLEAN with gates identical to baseline-next (runs/altuni-siblings-vs-baseline-next.txt). Conversion-only regression over all 149 styles of both batches (runs/altuni_regression.txt): 145 unchanged and 4 changed, namely these 3 (ONTO-RELEASE) and Kristi-Regular 784->742. Kristi's release has OS/2 v1, which carries no x-height; its harness gate is CLEAN and identical to baseline/ (runs/altuni-kristi/). The 10 standard-height tests and 113 fontforge tests pass, and cargo fmt --check and clippy are clean (runs/cargo-test-altuni.txt). verify_heights_port agrees 42/42.

Binary: /home/fsanches/compartilhado/sfd-reland-scratch/heights/bf-target/release/babelfont (runs/BF-ALTUNI.txt). fontforge_standard_height.rs is byte-identical at 119f2be and 17ea899, so the patch applies unchanged to #91.

proposed_tool_changes.description: New op 'addprivate <Key> <value...>'. It inserts 'BeginPrivate: 1 / <Key> <len> <value> / EndPrivate' where FontForge's SFD writer puts it: after DisplaySize/AntiAlias/FitToEm/WinInfo/OnlyBitmaps and before Grid/TeXData/AnchorClass2/BeginSubFonts/BeginChars (sfd.c SFDDumpPrivate, called from SFD_Dump). It is FATAL if the source already has a private dictionary, and it reports 'no private dictionary' as the before-state.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: make_edits.sh applies it to 13 sources, and each copy differs from its source by exactly the 3 added lines (runs/make_edits.txt). babelfont reads the section only for the height filter and does not emit it to .glyphs: the before->blues .glyphs diffs are the x/cap values only (runs/glyphs_diff-before-blues.txt).

decisions_for_felipe: Form of the 13 height edits. Recommended: (A) addprivate BlueValues, one edit per style. It restores the single input the exporter had, and the converter's own verified rule then yields both heights. The value comes from src/<X>.otf in the base tree. Alternative: (B) state the results with addfield OS2XHeight/OS2CapHeight, as the PatrickHand precedent did. That is 22 values, each derived by FontForge's rule with the .otf's BlueValues. Both close the same rows; only A was harness-run for all 13.

Restore only BlueValues (recommended and verified; the only private entry that affects a TTF export), or the whole CFF Private dict FontForge read from the .otf: OtherBlues, StdHW/StdVW, StemSnapH/V and so on. The other entries change nothing in the TTF, so they cannot be checked against the release.

Ledger: google/fonts 0436d99c0 and f8265bddf also bumped head.fontRevision and name to 1.002 and then 1.003. The gate does not block on these. Decide whether to add a setfield Version commit after the nbsp commit to mirror the bump, or leave it to future work.
Push the #91 follow-up commit (probes/babelfont-altuni-lookup.patch) to pr-ff-os2-defaults. kottaone, macondo and rosarivo cannot land CLEAN without it.
Commit the new sfd_edit.py op 'addprivate' (uncommitted in the working tree) together with investigations/next-heights/{probes,runs}. Nothing was committed, per the task.

The magra, rambla and rosarivo siblings (Magra-Regular, Rambla-Italic, Rambla-Regular, Rosarivo-Regular) also lost their BlueValues in the re-import, but they are CLEAN, so under the workspace rule they get no edit. Confirm that per-style asymmetry within a family is acceptable.
unresolved: Variation-sequence alternates are not modelled. FontForge's SCUniMatch compares alt->unienc even when the AltUni2 entry carries a variation selector, but babelfont's SFD reader leaves such entries out of glyph.codepoints. No style of either batch is affected (runs/altuni_regression.txt).
Lookup order: FontForge takes the lowest gid; babelfont (and the patch) takes file order. These are the same for FontForge-saved SFDs.

FontForge measured the unrounded in-memory quadratic splines after addExtrema/simplify/correctDirection (setquadraticaddextremasimplify-fontforge.py). classification_objections: The UNPAIRED row for TitilliumWeb-ExtraLight / -ExtraLightItalic is classified 'provenance'. The binary's provenance is certain: exported from src/TitilliumWeb-Thin(Italic)-TTF.sfd, with FFTM.sourceModified equal to its ModificationTime, byte-identical to hg, and confirmed by hg METADATA.json. The row is a gap in pair_next.py's rules, closed by the rule-4 tool change. In the precedent (PatrickHand), 'provenance' meant the release was not exported from the .sfd, which is not the case here.

Wallpoet name ID 4 is listed as unresolved because 'no converter-side fix restores Wallpoet'. That is false. fontc 1.0.0 applies a font-level 'Name Table Entry' custom parameter after building the names, and the '4; Wallpoet' variant built ID 4 'Wallpoet' (runs/psname_key_swap.txt). Like ID 6, it is converter-fidelity, not only compiler-derived.

Minor: the Titillium version row is a 'decision', which matches the tuffy precedent. But the unit's stated rule says any difference the release has and the source lacks must be a tool fix or a documented edit. Felipe should know the optional framing departs from that wording.
missed: Contour start point, a converter-fidelity issue in babelfont that the agent did not report. babelfont's model draws closed paths from nodes[0] (shape.rs to_kurbo). Its glyphs3 path conversion (shape.rs:696-735) copies node lists without rotating them. But Glyphs, glyphsLib and fontc treat the LAST node of a closed path as its start (glyphs2fontir toir.rs: 'the starting node of a closed contour is always stored at the end'). So every contour starts one node later than in FontForge's export: Wallpoet 394/394 rotated by 1; Titillium by 1 or 2 in every style (runs/start_point_rotation.txt). Traced on H in TitilliumWeb-Regular: the .sfd starts at (514,0), the .glyphs lists (514,0) first, and the build starts at (514,313). Rendering is unaffected. This explains the agent's unexplained Wallpoet fontspector change (outline_colinear_vectors / outline_short_segments WARN->PASS). The release has 49 FontForge closing duplicates (first point == last), which are not segments. The rotation moves them into the middle of the contour as zero-length segments. My emulation of colinear_vectors.rs gives 61 hits on the release (fontspector: WARN, 61 listed) and 112 on the build; above 100 the check returns PASS early. The 'better' status is therefore an artefact. Fix: rotate closed paths on write and read in the glyphs3 conversion; the same file as the PS-name PR, but a separate change.

The 3442 vs 3441 point count the agent left open: the only glyph that differs beyond the rotation is oslash. The build omits the on-curve (653,380), which is exactly the midpoint of its off-curve neighbours (645,384) and (661,376). The outline is identical (runs/point_counts_wallpoet.txt).

Wallpoet's release is hinted with the .sfd's own TrueType instructions: TtTable prep and fpgm, ShortTable cvt, gasp, and 178 glyph programs (180 TtInstrs/TtTable lines in Wallpoet-Regular-TTF.sfd). The build is unhinted. The gate accepts the prep/fpgm/cvt/gasp/glyf differences, and Puritan's FINDINGS notes the converter ignores instructions, but the unit's result never mentions it. Rendering on hinting rasterizers at small sizes differs, so it should be disclosed in Wallpoet's future_work / PR body. Titillium ships no glyph programs, so it is not affected.

The PS-name loss affects 16 landings, not 10, and UnifrakturMaguntia-Book is not landed: 9 CLEAN plus 7 CLEAN-UNPUBLISHED-CONVERTER (LovedbytheKing, OvertheRainbow, Ruluko-Regular, SwankyandMooMoo, TheGirlNextDoor, TitanOne-Regular, Trochut-Regular). I checked their baseline-next builds: ID 6 gains '-Regular' and ID 4 gains ' Regular'.

93550bd32 changed more than the unit's rows. It fixed name ID 4 spacing in all 11 styles ('Titillium WebBlack' -> 'Titillium Web Black'), restructured RIBBI names in 6 styles (IDs 1/2/16/17), removed ID 18 from Regular, and changed the fsSelection/macStyle bold bits of Black, SemiBold and SemiBoldItalic and the REGULAR bit of Light and ExtraLight. The build matches all of this only because fontc derives names and flags from the style, not because the sources say so (they still say 'Titillium WebBlack'). If the converter starts carrying FullName (for example the Name Table Entry route to fix Wallpoet's ID 4), 11 Titillium ID 4 rows appear and each needs a FullName edit citing 93550bd32. The ExtraLight-only FullName edit is also inconsistent with leaving the other 9 FullNames unedited.
fontspector version_bump was misread (see the version edit verdict): it PASSes 1.001 and does not show the downgrade.

The claim that there is no other source should cite upstream_info.md's ecm4u/Titillium. I checked it: it is the separate 'Titillium' family (Titillium-*.sfd, a mirror created in 2020), not Titillium Web, so the conclusion stands.
result.overall:
The investigation's core is correct and every number reproduced independently: the fsType release edits (93550bd32, 8ccda7bf7), the fontc weight-class gap, the ExtraLight <- Thin pairing, TTFWeight 275, the version option, and 11/11 plus 1/1 CLEAN, including the one-config family build. All six proposed .sfd edits hold; the values and origins are right and my candidates are byte-identical to the agent's.

Needs correction:
- The ExtraLight rename closes no gate row, and within it only FontName and LangName ID 3 affect this converter's build.
- The babelfont PS-name PR text: affected-landing count (16, not 10), environmental test failures that can be proven statically, integration tests not run, and name ID 4 is fixable through a Name Table Entry.
- The ExtraLight UNPAIRED row is a pairing-tool gap, not 'provenance'.
- Rule 4 should make its corroboration check mandatory.

Missed:
- babelfont's Glyphs start-node convention bug, which rotates every contour's start point. It explains the 'unresolved' Wallpoet fontspector change: 61 vs 112 colinear hits; the PASS is an artefact of the >100 early return.
- The oslash implied-point drop behind 3442 vs 3441.
- Wallpoet's dropped source-stated TrueType hinting, which should be disclosed.
- A version_bump misreading.

Kerning, which the gate never shapes for GPOS-shipping styles, is now verified: all pairs of all 11 Titillium styles position identically. Neither landing is blocked; both remain *-UNPUBLISHED-CONVERTER until babelfont #91/#92/#93 merge.

rows.cause: NOT an empty GPOS: the task premise is wrong for this style. The release has no GPOS, GSUB or GDEF, only a legacy `kern` table (format 0, 3904 pairs). FontForge v20110222 wrote it with OpenType output off. The FFTM stamp 3381227313 minus 2082844800 = 1298382513, exactly LibFF_ModTime of the v20110222 tarball. The hg binary at 52f780bc already has this layout; google/fonts hotfix 0e5ac906d changed only head/name. In tottf.c:5306, initATTables writes `kern` only when neither applemode nor opentypemode is set. Our build kerns through GPOS, because fontc cannot write a legacy `kern`. The gate's arbitrate_legacy_kern refuses because 28 pairs whose first glyph is U+00AD shape differently. HarfBuzz's kern-table machine puts kern1=v>>1 on the hidden soft hyphen's advance, which is then zeroed, and kern2 on the next glyph. GPOS puts the whole value on the hidden glyph, so the next glyph does not move. No combining marks, so fallback positioning plays no part. The empty-GPOS tool change cannot touch this row.

proposed_tool_changes.description: An opt-in shared GSUB/GPOS script list, default off. fea-rs gets Opts::share_script_lists(bool). After AllLookups::build assigns features, every script present in either table is added to the other with an empty default LangSys (0xFFFF, no features) if it is missing; a table's own languages are untouched. PosSubBuilder::build_raw no longer returns None when scripts exist, so a table with scripts but no features or lookups is written. fontir gets Flags::SHARED_LAYOUT_SCRIPTS, fontbe passes it to the feature compile (on main, both compile and compile_merged), and the fontc CLI gets --shared-layout-scripts. This is VOLT's convention and FontForge's exporter rule (lookups.c SFScriptsInLookups/SFLangsInScript, tottfgpos.c dumpg___info, unchanged from 2010 to master 67dd7dc9). proposed_tool_changes.description: FEA forbids script/language statements inside aalt, so aalt is registered under every `languagesystem`. FontForge registers it only where its aalt lookups say. decisions_for_felipe: Mechanism for the empty GPOS: a fontc opt-in flag plus a builder3 config key (prototyped, clean, 2 PRs plus a fontc release), or a builder3-only post-compile op (1 PR, not prototyped). Either way nothing lands until it is merged and released, since land.py refuses forks. The PRs are yours to file.

Reproducing the shell turns HarfBuzz's fallback mark positioning OFF, as the release does, for Varela's 3 and UnifrakturMaguntia's 9 combining marks. Arguably worse rendering, but it is what ships. Dropping sharedLayoutScripts could be a later improvement commit (future_work).

Smokum and Ultra are not empty-GPOS cases. FontForge exported them with no GPOS, only a legacy kern table, and fontc can only kern through GPOS. Options: accept GPOS kerning with documented HarfBuzz differences (Smokum: 28 soft-hyphen pairs; Ultra: 2211 mark pairs plus 17 soft-hyphen pairs, after the class-0 edit), or hold them. The only exact route is a builder3 op that writes `kern` and drops GPOS. It was not prototyped and is unlikely to be accepted upstream (fontspector flags fonts without GPOS kerning).

Miama and Nosifer landed CLEAN, but their marks shape differently from the release (73,515 and 1,968 LTR pairs), because the gate's legacy-kern rule does not look at fallback mark positioning. Re-open them, or accept under the same decision as Smokum/Ultra? And should the gate be tightened?

Ultra's source postdates its release (.sfd saved 2011-10-18, export of the 2011-05-03 state). Should it take the TTFWeight 400 and Weight Regular edits (values from the release/hg binary)? Without the first, land.py's weight workaround opens OS/2.us_weight_class [400,900] (runs/16).

tool_verdicts.reason: The patch is fine (tree cc6eaf66; built as 4b375fa3 and it works). One point the other agent did not report: FontcConfig and GoogleFontsOptions do not deny unknown fields. So on any builder3 before this change, including the prebuilt main-latest binary the landed repos' CI downloads (.github/workflows/build.yaml), `sharedLayoutScripts: true` is silently ignored and the font is built without the shell, with no error. Separately, the Python gftools builder's GOOGLEFONTS_SCHEMA rejects the key ('unexpected key not in schema', tested with the local gftools 0.9.100.dev). The landing and verification must therefore check the built GPOS shell, not trust the key, and must refuse builder3 revisions that lack the change.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs make_langsys exclude_dflt for non-dflt languages
tool_verdicts.reason: This is a correct fidelity fix: FontForge registers each lookup for exactly the languages it names. The patch was reproduced (tree 1dc7e1d1). With both babelfont commits, Varela's GSUB effects go from 7 of 161 differing keys to 0 of 160, fi does not ligate under tr/az/crh, and Poly-Italic and Poly-Regular are CLEAN. The PROTOTYPE commit author/subject ('scratch <scratch@localhost>') needs replacing before the PR.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs declare only aalt's languagesystems when there is no kerning and no anchors
tool_verdicts.reason: It works. Reproduced: Varela GSUB 3->0 together with exclude_dflt, aalt no longer under latn/SRB ('!' stays exclam under sr), Poly-Italic 3->0 and Poly-Regular still CLEAN. It is the only FEA-expressible route, because aalt forbids script/language statements. It is a conditional heuristic that falls back to a warning when kerning or anchors exist, so upstream acceptance is medium. The PR text should say plainly that it relies on explicit `script`/`language` statements for undeclared language systems, which fea-rs accepts.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: sfd-reland recipe/baseline/land: sharedLayoutScripts for FFTM + empty GPOS + GSUB with lookups (narrow rule)
tool_verdicts.reason: The rule selects exactly the 5 empty-GPOS releases (my independent census agrees), and Kristi and Lekton-Regular stay CLEAN with the exact shell (runs/12). Because builder3 silently ignores the key, verify_landed.py and land.py must assert that the built font has the GPOS or GSUB shell and must pin a builder3 that has the change. Otherwise a CI or rebuild on current builder3 produces a font without the shell and nothing notices.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: table_gate arbitrate_legacy_kern: account for fallback mark positioning and shape the full pair matrix
tool_verdicts.reason: The code (table_gate.py 1250-1313 at 2f43693) shapes only the release's own kern pairs and compares advance sums, so mark fallback differences are invisible to it. I reproduced Nosifer's fidelity-only build: 1,975 of 110,224 LTR pairs differ, 1,968 of them involving marks.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: sfd-reland tools/sfd_edit.py kernclass0zero op
tool_verdicts.reason: It is not needed. The A-group row it removes is not in the .sfd Ultra was exported from (2d042ebbd). Fix the pairing instead.

classification_objections: Ultra-Regular GPOS.script_list/feature_list/lookup_list: keeping these as 'decision' (kern-only release) is right, but the cause text is wrong in two places. The A-group kerning (650 pairs) is attributed to FontForge's class-0 decompose rule, but the exported .sfd had no kern classes. The source is described as postdating the export, as if the exported state were unknown, but it is in googlefontdirectory-hg history at 2d042ebbd. The HarfBuzz statement in the fontc patch's doc comment and commit message is false (see the tool verdict), and it would be the first thing an upstream reviewer checks.
builder3 silently ignores unknown config keys, and the Python gftools builder rejects `sharedLayoutScripts`. The recipe's config key is therefore not self-enforcing.

The builder3 prototype binary (734e373e) used for runs/04, 10 and 15 was built 44 minutes before fontc commit 0df9f5ee existed, so it came from an uncommitted working tree. Results reproduce from the committed patch (my build 4b375fa3), so only the pin in the verification section is wrong.
result.overall:
The investigation holds up for Varela, UnifrakturMaguntia and Smokum, but not for Ultra.

For Varela and UnifrakturMaguntia, the causes are right: FontForge's shared GSUB/GPOS script list, a fea-rs gap, and babelfont's include_dflt and aalt registration. I rebuilt the fontc/builder3 and babelfont prototypes from the patch files and they reproduce every claimed outcome. Varela is CLEAN with all prototypes, UnifrakturMaguntia keeps only its 2 first-batch vmetric rows, Poly is CLEAN, Kristi and Lekton-Regular are CLEAN with the exact shell, and horizontal pair differences go to 0. Two things need fixing before any PR is filed:
- The fontc patch text wrongly says HarfBuzz ignores a legacy `kern` table whenever a GPOS exists.
- The builder3 key is silently ignored by current builder3 and rejected by the Python builder, so landing and verification must check the built shell.

Smokum is correctly identified as a kern-only release, and its U+00AD analysis is right.

Ultra is where the result is wrong. The three proposed .sfd edits (TTFWeight 400, Weight Regular, kernclass0zero) should be rejected. The release was exported from googlefontdirectory-hg 2d042ebbd's Ultra-TTF.sfd, an exact FFTM ModificationTime match, and that file needs no edit at all: weight 400, Weight Book with correct Regular names, per-glyph kerning with no A-group, and .null/nonmarkingreturn present. The pairing uses the October 2011 re-save instead, and the A-group kerning was added in that re-save, not dropped by FontForge. What remains for Ultra is the same decision as Smokum (GPOS kerning versus a legacy-kern release): 2211 mark pairs and 17 soft-hyphen pairs.

landable_after: varela and poly, once the babelfont PR merges; varela additionally needs the fontc release and builder3 PR. unifraktur still needs the vmetric rule. smokum, and ultra re-paired to 2d042ebbd, need Felipe's kern-only decision.

That commit is the lohit-gujarati-2.92.1 tag (2013-12-12), which a 'tag_match' heuristic took from another family in the monorepo. The release was built from the 0df83ad state. rows.row: RENDERING (not a table-gate row): 284 Bengali words differ, up to 801 px, while the table gate reports CLEAN
rows.cause: Below- and above-base marks are not positioned (u09C1, u09C2, u09C3, u0981, reph). The release's GPOS is abvm = [mark-to-base with 240 bases, chain lookup 2] and blwm = [mark-to-base]. babelfont leaves the .sfd's anchor lookups to fontc's mark writer, but it writes the chain lookup "'abvm' Above Base Mark in Bengali lookup 2" as a declared feature abvm. fontc does not generate a feature the source already declares, so our GPOS is abvm = [chain] and mark = 3 mark-to-base lookups with only 5 bases (uni25CC and glyphNNN). The table gate calls the GPOS difference RELEASE-STALE ('organised differently'), and neither baseline.sh nor land.py gates the rendering diff. The fault is in the converter, not in the pairing: the same 288 words differ at a403c9b.
rows.evidence: d3 locations of runs r0/r1/r2/r5 (probes/d3_render.py): 288 -> 284 -> 284 words. With a '# Automatic Code' marker added to abvm, 117 words remain (runs/r4-lohit-bengali-marker, probes/mark_feature_marker.sh): fontc then builds abvm with 50/50/37 bases and no blwm.

rows.cause: babelfont's SFD reader gives every GlyphClass:4 glyph the Glyphs subCategory Nonspacing (fontforge.rs, upstream since #66). fontc exports a Nonspacing mark with zero width (glyphs-reader 1.0.0 Glyph::is_nonspacing_mark; glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 source.rs:1829). FontForge writes the advance the source states (Width 532/776). A Mark with subCategory Spacing Combining keeps both its GDEF mark class (category_for_glyph_preliminary) and its advance.
rows.evidence: The prototype (probes/babelfont-spacing-combining-mark.patch) takes rows from 2 to 0 CLEAN with 0 glyph and 0 word rendering diffs (runs/r2-lohit-spacingmark, runs/r5-lohit-final). probes/advancing_marks.py (runs/advancing_marks.txt) finds only Lohit-Tamil and Cardo-Italic/Regular affected.

rows.row: cmap x458 LOST (U+0021-U+007E, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Greek, SF*/SM*/SS*/SV* box drawing, U+FB00-FB04 ...)
rows.cause: The Latin comes from the build script, not from the .sfd. build.py (helper.py in the 0.02 ChangeLog) runs font.mergeFonts('cour/cour.pfa') (courb.pfa for Bold), which adds the IBM Courier Type 1 fonts in src/cour/. The .sfd has no Latin: the 2008-08-09 ChangeLog says 'Removed non-arabic glyphs'. FontForge 2008 _MergeFont (fvfonts.c at eb711fd7) copies glyphs unscaled: A has advance 600 in the 1024-em font. It names them by FontForge's own UniFromName (namelist.c psaltnames: SM680000->U+2310, ohm->U+2126, micro->U+00B5, dbar->U+0111, Pts->U+20A7). fontTools' AGL leaves 33 of these different.

rows.row: GSUB.script_list, GSUB.feature_list, GSUB.lookup_list (release: rlig/init/medi/fina/liga arab + liga latn; ours: none)
rows.cause: Five of the six lookups come from build.py's font.mergeFeature('Thabit.fea'): rligTashkilLigatures, InitialForms, MedialForms, FinalForms and ligaLamAlef. The sixth is a latn liga lookup that FontForge's AFM reader created from the IBM Courier AFM's L lines (LoadKerningDataFromAfm). The release's PfEd names that lookup "Courier-'liga' Standard Ligatures in Latin lookup 0". Its rules equal X.Org font-ibm-type1 cour.afm ('N f ; L f ff ; L i fi ; L l fl', 'N ff ; L i ffi ; L l ffl'). The AFMs are not in the hg tree.
rows.evidence: Rows go from 3 to 0 with mergefea plus mergepsfont with the AFM (runs/t2, runs/p3); PfEd decoded in-session; runs/thabit_release_inputs.txt

rows.cause: fontc 1.0.0 ignores a single master's instance weightClass. The .sfd states TTFWeight 500 or 700. This is the known issue in issues/fontc-static-weight-class.md.
rows.evidence: Closed by land.py's workaround as applied by probes/rebuild_with_workarounds.sh: rows go from 3 to 2 for each style (runs/p3/workarounds)

rows.cause: PfEd is FontForge's private table. In these releases it holds only the GSUB/GPOS lookup, subtable and anchor-class names (decoded: rligTashkilLigatures, ... "Courier-'liga' ...", ArabicAbove, ...). No shaper or rasterizer reads it, fontc does not write it, and the gate already accepts FontForge's other private table, FFTM.
rows.evidence: probes/table_gate_ff_private.py takes each style from 2 rows to 0 (runs/p3/gate-ff-private)

rows.cause: FontForge 2008 tottf.c sethead writes 0 for a font with both LTR and RTL glyphs ('if ( lr && rl ) head->dirhint = 0;'); Thabit is Arabic plus Courier. The OpenType spec deprecates the field ('set to 2'), no Glyphs parameter can state it, and fontc writes 2. The same row appears for Cardo-Bold and Cardo-Italic (Hebrew plus Latin).
rows.evidence: tottf.c at fontforge eb711fd7 lines 2777-2783; probes/table_gate_ff_private.py gives 0 rows

rows.cause: The .sfd has no .notdef. FontForge's TTF exporter synthesises one (tottf.c dumpmissingglyph): stem = (a+d)/30 = 34, ymax = 682, xmax = 306, advance 374. That is exactly the release's glyph. This is the same rule as the Tuffy precedent.
rows.evidence: The ffnotdef emulation (probes/ff_build_ops.py) removes the .notdef member: hmtx.2 becomes hmtx.1 (runs/t1-thabit-merged vs t1-thabit-merged-notdef)

rows.cause: The .sfd states half-unit points (186.5 0 m). FontForge's SSAddPoints writes glyf points with rint(), which rounds ties to even (186). fontc rounds half up (187). There are 1574 half-unit coordinates in 102 glyphs.
rows.evidence: The prototype filter --fontforge-rint-coordinates takes rows from 4 (runs/t6) to 3 (runs/t7) and clears dalring U+0689's 80-px rendering diff

rows.row: 44 Arabic words: lam-alef not formed across harakat, marks unattached on lam-alef ligatures
rows.cause: Two converter defects. (a) babelfont writes lookupflag only for contextual lookups (the has_chain branch, upstream since #78), so ligaLamAlef loses RightToLeft|IgnoreMarks (SFD flag 9) and every ordinary GSUB/GPOS lookup loses its flags. (b) babelfont names 'baselig <n>' anchors with the bare class name, which duplicates it, so fontc cannot build mark-to-ligature. Glyphs names them <class>_<n+1>.
rows.evidence: Arabic word diffs go from 44 (runs/t4) through the lookupflag prototype (runs/t5, max 351 -> 269 px) to 0 with the baselig prototype added (runs/t6). Patches: probes/babelfont-lookupflag-all-lookups.patch, probes/babelfont-baselig-anchor-names.patch.

rows.row: 1 Arabic word: shaddahdammah attached to uniFBFE in ours, not in the release
rows.cause: In Thabit-Bold.sfd uniFBFE is only a reference (to gid 179) and has no anchors. FontForge exports a glyph's own anchors only. fontc propagates anchors from components unless the font sets the custom parameter 'Propagate Anchors' to false.
rows.evidence: The prototype filter --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation takes this from 1 word to 0 (runs/p2 -> runs/p3)

rows.cause: FontForge's dumpanchor writes anchors with putshort(gpos, ap->me.x), which truncates toward zero. fontc rounds. The skew makes every anchor fractional.
rows.evidence: With --fontforge-truncate-anchors every remaining Arabic word diff has identical glyphs and positions: 6/6 and 7/7 (runs/p2, runs/p3)

rows.row: 60-83 Latin/Greek/symbol glyph diffs (<=46 px) and 121-140 Latin words (<=108 px)
rows.cause: FontForge's merge converts each copied Type 1 glyph to the order2 layer with splineorder2.c SplineSetsTTFApprox (fvfonts.c SplineCharCopy -> SCConvertOrder). The mergepsfont probe uses cu2qu (max_err 1) instead, so the points differ from FontForge's and the areas differ by up to 0.2% (e.g. 'o' 71478 vs 71613). Contour reversal (psread.c) and naming are exact.
rows.evidence: runs/p3/SUMMARY.txt; the Arabic has 0 glyph diffs in the uprights

rows.row: no source (UNPAIRED); against the upright source: 465 rows each
rows.cause: The obliques are generated at build time: build.py obliqize() then deobliqize() then generate() with couri.pfa or courbi.pfa. The release confirms every step. The skew is psMat.skew(-16) in RADIANS, x' = x - 0.30063 y; measured -0.3007. U+200C..U+202E (afii61664..afii61575) are deselected and stay upright. References are unlinked. Upright Courier ( ) [ ] { } ! are pasted in, and the release shows them unskewed with the upright lsb. PfEd names the lookup "Courier-Italic-'liga'..." (Courier-BoldItalic in BoldOblique).
rows.evidence: The upright source gives 465 rows (runs/o0-obliques-upright-source). The generated sources give 3 rows (runs/o7, runs/p3), 2 with land.py's workaround and 0 with the gate change; the Arabic GSUB/GPOS shaping is identical.

rows.row: 1 and 15 Arabic glyph diffs; 6 and 7 Arabic words whose shaping is identical
rows.cause: This is a release inconsistency no source can reproduce. FontForge 2008 writes the glyf bbox from curve extrema and the hmtx lsb as the unrounded minx truncated to int (tottf.c ttfdumpmetrics putshort(gi->hmtx, b->minx)). As a result 156 and 228 glyphs carry an lsb different from their own xMin. Examples: kafinitial has lsb -56 with xMin -57; tehring has header xMin -29 while its points reach -32. A rasterizer places the glyph by the lsb, so it draws one unit off. Our point sets are identical to the release's (kafinitial 41 = 41 points).
rows.evidence: probes/stale_lsb.py (runs/stale_lsb.txt): every Arabic glyph diff is a stale-lsb glyph

rows.row: family 'Regular Medium'/'Bold' in our build vs 'Thabit' in the release; copyright, designer and name IDs 8/9/16/18
rows.cause: The .sfd drifted after the release, and the release's own source state is lost. Shipped Thabit.ttf is byte-identical to the Arabeyes Thabit-0.02 release (SourceForge Fonts/Thabit 0.02/Thabit-0.02.tar.gz, built 2008-08-09). The other three styles differ from that release only in name ID 4 (Raph Levien's FixName, hg 465c5490a + 49339cae0, 2011-12-15). The hg .sfd files were saved again on 2010-06-15 (ModificationTime 1276640170 / 1276640219), with Copyright 2008-2010, FamilyName 'Regular'/'Bold' and new LangName credits. The ChangeLog is unchanged since 0.02, and the drawing is unchanged: 0 Arabic rendering diffs in the uprights. The 2008-08-09 .sfd has not been found anywhere: not in hg, not in the repo archive, and the SourceForge tarballs ship only TTFs.

rows.cause: The file is not an SFD. It is a Type 1 PFB ('%!PS-AdobeFont-1.0: Yellowtail 001.001', 'Generated by FontForge 20110222', Creator Dave Crossland, CreationDate Mon Jul 18 09:51:27 2011); babelfont reports 'Not an SFD file'. proposed_sfd_edits.commit_body:
google/fonts ships Limelight-Regular.ttf as googlefontdirectory 927784141
(Dave Crossland, 2012-08-20) added it. Its vertical metrics were changed
after FontForge exported it from this source: head.created keeps the export
time (2012-04-07), head.modified says 2012-08-20, and the glyph boxes were
recomputed over all points. FontForge exports this source with typo, win
and hhea ascent 1881, win descent 631 and hhea descender -632; the release
has 1864, 629 and -629, the integer part of the outlines' extremes (1864.0,
-629.28), as the repository's tools/bbox/vmetcheck.py prescribed. The typo
descender stays -634, as in the release. Stated absolutely.
proposed_sfd_edits.value_derived_from: Copied from the release, and disclosed as such: google/fonts b5efa9c32e8f ofl/limelight/Limelight-Regular.ttf, blob 879e7f9d, identical to googlefontdirectory-hg 927784141. These values are a post-export edit. They equal int() of this source's true outline extremes (max 1864.0 on uni1E1F, min -629.28 on kcommaaccent), the rule of googlefontdirectory-hg 927784141:tools/bbox/vmetcheck.py. So they can be derived from the source outlines as well as read from the release. The typo descender the edit left alone (-634) is not touched here.
proposed_sfd_edits.source_currently_states: OS2TypoAscent: 243 / OS2TypoAOffset: 1, OS2WinAscent: 17 / OS2WinAOffset: 1, OS2WinDescent: 3 / OS2WinDOffset: 1, HheadAscent: 17 / HheadAOffset: 1, HheadDescent: -3 / HheadDOffset: 1. These are offsets, which FontForge 20090914 exports as 1881 / 1881 / 631 / 1881 / -632, the designer's intent: the designer's own src/Limelight-Regular.otf carries 1881/-634 in typo, win and hhea.

proposed_tool_changes.description: A new opt-in filter, --fontforge-legacy-offset-metrics, in the 'reproducing a legacy FontForge export' group. It re-resolves a FontForge source's offset-mode usWinAscent, usWinDescent and hhea ascender/descender against the bases FontForge's exporter used before ee15007274e9 (2014-09-16). Win: floor/ceil of each glyph's ON-CURVE points over decomposed default-master layers; the SFD reader keeps every SplinePoint, including interpolated quadratic ones, as an on-curve node. hhea: the true outline extremes truncated toward zero, widened to that box, and to 0 when a glyph is empty. The reader also records each metric's stated delta (format_specific 'sfd.offset_delta.<key>') so the filter does not depend on the reader's own base rule. After resolving, the filter marks the metric absolute (offset flag '0', offset_mode marker removed), so an SFD write-back stays consistent. The #85 default (floor/ceil of the true outline) is unchanged. The prototype adds 319 lines: 9 in fontforge.rs, 1 in filters/mod.rs, and the new filters/fontforgelegacyoffsetmetrics.rs with 3 unit tests.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Harness, rows before -> after: MountainsofChristmas-Bold 4 -> 1 (runs/02; the remaining row is us_weight_class) -> 0 with land.py's workarounds (runs/03). NothingYouCouldDo 2 -> 0 (runs/02). MountainsofChristmas-Regular stays 0 (runs/02). UnifrakturMaguntia-Book, the precedent, 5 -> 3, with only the GPOS shell left (runs/05 -> runs/06). Conversion sweep over all 149 styles of families.tsv + families-next.tsv (runs/proto_metrics_sweep.txt): six metrics per style match the release 851 times with the filter vs 844 without, and the filter changes exactly 4 styles (UnifrakturMaguntia-Book, MountainsofChristmas-Bold, NothingYouCouldDo, Limelight-Regular). No value moves away from its release. The model sweep (runs/offset_bases_sweep.txt, 328 offset-mode metrics in 82 styles, all quadratic): pre-2014 rule 305, #85 298, FontForge-master rule 295. The pre-2014 rule never misses a metric #85 gets. Its 23 misses are Limelight (release edit), Play-Bold (no FFTM) and Puritan (em scale, its own plan). The PR #85 evidence pairs (hg -TTF .sfd vs GF release, runs/offset_bases_pr85_evidence.txt): the pre-2014 rule gets copse, daysone and handlee 12/12, #85 8/12. copse ships 1991, not the 1992 #85's message claims; sfd-batch5/tools/probes/sfd_bbox_rounding/README.md recorded that before #85 merged. edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Merge Thabit.fea into the source, as build.py does
edit_verdicts.reason: Verified. build.py merges the feature file before the fonts (font.mergeFeature(fea), then font.mergeFonts). FontForge 2008's fea_ParseLookupFlags accepts the comma-separated 'RightToLeft, IgnoreMarks', so ligaLamAlef gets flag 9. The release's GSUB is 5 arab lookups with flags 1,1,1,1,9 plus the latn liga, and PfEd names them '<name>' / '<name> subtable'. My w2 build reproduces the GSUB lookup for lookup (runs/w2/Thabit.layout.txt vs runs/thabit_release_layout.txt). The op still has to be added to tools/sfd_edit.py.

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Add the IBM Courier AFMs FontForge read beside cour/*.pfa
edit_verdicts.reason: Keep as decision D3. It is inferred, but the inference holds. In FontForge 2008, SCLigDefault is commented out (fvfonts.c:876, splineutil.c:2473), so a liga lookup can only come from an AFM (CheckAfmOfPostscript). I fetched the X.Org 88a51da files myself: the PFAs are byte-identical to hg's, cour.afm has exactly the 5 'L' ligatures and 0 KPX (the release has no kern), and PfEd names the lookup "Courier-'liga' Standard Ligatures in Latin lookup 0".

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Merge IBM Courier into the source, as build.py does
edit_verdicts.reason: The op claims to follow _MergeFont, but its worth-outputting test is 'draws or is referenced'. FontForge's SCWorthOutputting is draws || widthset || anchor || dependents (splinesaveafm.c:1063), so the op drops Courier's blank 'spacenumeric' (600, unencoded). FontForge copied that glyph: the release has 788 glyphs = 308-1+478+3. The gate calls it unreachable, so it does not block, but the op is not exact. Separately, the cu2qu stand-in leaves 60-83 Latin glyph diffs (up to 46 px) and about 148 word diffs per style (runs/w1/SUMMARY.txt). The edit is therefore not yet functionally equivalent (D5).

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Generate the oblique sources as build.py does
edit_verdicts.reason: The ops reproduce the skew and the paste, but not obliqize()'s naming step: fontname+'-Oblique', fullname+' Oblique', familyname, and the Arabic SubFamily name. FontForge 2008 derived macStyle italic from 'Obli' in the name (macbinary.c _MacStyleCode). The release obliques therefore carry fsSelection ITALIC and macStyle 2/3. Our builds come out named 'Regular Medium'/'Regular' and 'Bold'/'Bold', the same as the uprights, with fsSelection REGULAR+USE_TYPO_METRICS or BOLD, macStyle 0/1 and PS names Regular-Medium/Bold-Bold (runs/style_bits_hidden.txt). METADATA wants post_script_name Thabit-Oblique / Thabit-Bold-Oblique and style italic. The gate hides all of this because it accepts OS/2.fs_selection and head.mac_style wholesale and does not gate names. Even with FontName Thabit-Oblique set, babelfont+fontc give fsSelection REGULAR and macStyle 0 (runs/v6-oblique-named/style_flags.txt), so a converter rule (FontForge's name-derived italic) or an explicit style edit is also needed.

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Credit IBM for the Latin, as build.py does
edit_verdicts.reason: The body says 'the release's name ID 0 carries it', but applying the 2010 build.py text to the 2010 copyright does not give the release's string. The edit would give 'Typeface and data (C) 2008-2010, Khaled Hosny.\nThis font ... license.\nLatin glyphs are ...'. The release's name ID 0 is 'Typeface and data (C) 2002-2008, Khaled Hosny.This font is distributed under the terms of OFL license. Latin glyphs are Copyright (c) IBM Corporation 1990,1991.': different years, and a space separator. Either restore the release string and say it comes from the binary, as the FamilyName edit does, or drop the edit as not functional. It is marked unverified and should stay so.

tool_verdicts.reason: Confirmed: parse_anchor only prefixes '_' for 'mark' and leaves baselig anchors with the bare class name, which duplicates it (fontforge.rs parse_anchor; unchanged upstream). The Glyphs _1/_2 convention is what fontc's mark-to-ligature writer needs.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs filter --fontforge-rint-coordinates
tool_verdicts.reason: Confirmed. tottf.c SSAddPoints writes bp = rint(...). The release has uni06D4 at 186/236/450/400 from .sfd 186.5/236.5/450.5/400.5, all even, which is ties-to-even.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs filter --fontforge-implied-oncurves
tool_verdicts.reason: The filter models only the path where the stored numbering is valid, dropping points with ttfindex -1 that pass SPInterpolate. When SCPointsNumberedProperly fails (splinechar.c:368, e.g. a glyph with both references and splines, or with stale numbers), tottf.c:1366-1370 renumbers with SSTtfNumberPoints. That path drops every SPInterpolate-able on-curve point, including ones with a stored ttfindex, which the filter keeps. Implement the renumbering case or document the limitation before upstreaming.

tool_verdicts.reason: Confirmed: tottfgpos.c dumpanchor calls putshort(gpos, ap->me.x) with a float, which truncates.

tool_verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Thabit-Bold.sfd's uniFBFE is only 'Refer: 179' with no AnchorPoint, while the Regular has its own. fontc honours 'Propagate Anchors' (glyphs-reader 1.0.0 font.rs:1164, glyphs2fontir source.rs:190).

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs: write FontForge's anchor mark lookups explicitly (Lohit-Bengali)
tool_verdicts.reason: The agent missed that babelfont ALREADY inserts an insertion marker into declared abvm/blwm/kern/dist/mark/mkmk features: fontforge.rs:3759 statements.insert(0, "# Automatic code start"), Simon's 66334a7a, still present on upstream main 91bf8bb. fea-rs 1.0.0 honours only a comment that starts with '# Automatic Code' (token_tree/typed.rs:768, case-sensitive), so the marker is ignored. The first, upstream-mergeable step is to fix that string. Rewriting only the marker text in the converted .glyphs (probes/marker_case_fix.sh) gives exactly the agent's r4 result: 284 -> 117 words (runs/v2-bengali-marker-casefix). The remaining 117 come from fontc's mark writer. is_below_mark needs anchor names starting 'bottom' or 'nukta' (fontbe marks.rs:784), but the SFD classes are Anchor-0/1/2, so no blwm is built. Bases are also filtered to abvm-script glyphs: 50/50/37 against the release's 240/253. The explicit-lookup design is only needed for that remainder.

classification_objections: Lohit-Bengali rendering (converter-fidelity): the class is right but the cause is incomplete. The 'declared abvm suppresses fontc's writer' effect comes from a mis-cased marker babelfont already emits: '# Automatic code start' against fea-rs's case-sensitive '# Automatic Code'. That is a one-line upstream bug, not a missing feature. Only the remaining 117 words need the explicit-lookup design.

Lohit-Tamil is called landable ('CLEAN, 0 glyph and 0 word rendering diffs'), but it is not functionally equivalent. The build sets fsSelection USE_TYPO_METRICS, while the release (OS/2 v1) does not. FontForge only sets bit 7 when the OS/2 version it writes is 4 or more (tottf.c eb711fd7 lines 3283-3289); babelfont maps OS2_UseTypoMetrics unconditionally. For Tamil, apps that honour the bit switch line spacing from win 866/363 to typo 1400/-648/+20. The table gate hides this by accepting OS/2.fs_selection wholesale. It is a converter-fidelity row; runs/v5-tamil-no-typo-bit shows fs_selection [64,192] goes away when the bit is not set.

Thabit-Oblique and Thabit-BoldOblique: '3 rows, 2 with land.py's workaround, 0 with the gate change' is only a table-gate result. The generated sources lose the release's ITALIC style bit (fsSelection 1 -> REGULAR+USE_TYPO_METRICS; macStyle 2 -> 0, 3 -> 1) and are named 'Regular Medium' / 'Bold' like the uprights. This is functional (style linking, METADATA style italic and PS name) and is not the 'names; not gated' provenance row. Part of it is provenance (build.py's naming step was not reproduced), and part is converter fidelity (FontForge's name-derived italic).

Thabit (all four styles), 'rows_after 0 with the gate change': land.py would still refuse every style. The build GAINS U+00A0 (glyph uni00A0, the last glyph, gid 307/309, of both 2010 .sfd files). The release neither encodes nor contains that glyph, so the 2010 save introduced it. The table gate accepts gained codepoints, but land.py's cmap_difference requires the release's exact codepoints. This is a provenance row with no edit proposed.

Yellowtail: 'google/fonts 1baf54ea4 changed only name IDs 3/4/5/6 and head.modified/fontRevision' is imprecise. The cmap table bytes also changed; the mappings are identical, so this is a re-encoding and functionally irrelevant.
missed: Thabit, Thabit-Bold, Thabit-Oblique, Thabit-BoldOblique: GAINED U+00A0. The agent's own p3 gate prints it ('our uni00A0 (an addition at U+00A0...)') but the report never mentions it. Our builds have 786 glyphs against the release's 788 = 308-1+478+3, and uni00A0 is the only glyph the release lacks. It is empty, Width 637, 'Flags: HW', and last in both .sfd files; nothing refers to it. FontForge 2008 would have exported it (SCWorthOutputting counts widthset), so the release's 2008 source did not contain it. Proposed documented edit: 'Drop uni00A0, which the 2010 save added', a new sfd_edit op dropglyph. Origin: the release's cmap and glyph set, and its position as the last gid. Measured with DROP_NBSP=1 (probes/thabit_pipeline_verify.sh, runs/w2): codepoints become exactly the release's in all 4 styles, with no change to rows or rendering (runs/w1_w2_cmap_exactness.txt).

Thabit obliques: build.py's obliqize() naming step (fontname/fullname/familyname and the Arabic SubFamily) and FontForge 2008's name-derived italic (macbinary.c _MacStyleCode: 'Obli' -> sf_italic, which becomes fsSelection ITALIC) are not reproduced. Ours is not italic and is named like the upright (runs/style_bits_hidden.txt). Setting FontName Thabit-Oblique alone is not enough; babelfont+fontc still give REGULAR/macStyle 0 (runs/v6-oblique-named). A babelfont rule is needed to mark the instance italic, as FontForge did when the source states no MacStyle.

A converter-fidelity rule for all FontForge-exported styles with OS/2 version < 4: do not set USE_TYPO_METRICS (FontForge tottf.c: only 'if ( os2->version>=4 )'). It affects Lohit-Tamil (typo 1400/-648/20 vs win 866/363), Lohit-Bengali (750/-274/0 vs 760/325), Thabit and Thabit-Oblique (819/0/900 vs 983/528). It is hidden by table_gate.py ACCEPTED['OS/2']['fs_selection'] ('USE_TYPO_METRICS is set by the build'), even though the conversion, not the build, sets it from a flag FontForge ignored. It is probably programme-wide, beyond this unit.

babelfont's existing insertion marker is mis-cased: fontforge.rs:3759 '# Automatic code start', upstream Simon 66334a7a, still on main 91bf8bb. fea-rs requires '# Automatic Code'. This one-line fix is the upstream-mergeable first step for Lohit-Bengali, 284 -> 117 words (runs/v2-bengali-marker-casefix). It probably affects every SFD that declares abvm/blwm/mark/mkmk/kern/dist through a chain or other lookup.

The regression sweeps (probes/sweep_summary.py) compare verdict and row COUNTS only. A patch that closes one row and opens another in the same style is invisible there, as the Cardo-Italic +2/-4 case shows; the 'no table-row regressions' claim is weaker than stated.
mergepsfont omits Courier's blank 'spacenumeric', which FontForge merged because it is widthset (unencoded, 600). It is harmless (the gate calls it unreachable), but the op does not match _MergeFont.
result.overall:
The provenance findings hold up. Lohit's METADATA commit a403c9b is another family's tag, and the FFTM stamps pin Bengali to 0df83ad and Tamil to 361b23b. Thabit is the build.py output: the 2010 .sfd plus Thabit.fea, IBM Courier and the X.Org AFMs, with generated obliques. Yellowtail's '.sfd' is a Type 1 PFB. I checked every FontForge-exporter rule the agent cites against the eb711fd7 sources, and every babelfont reader defect is still present on upstream main 91bf8bb.

The report overstates what lands. Four functional gaps are missed, and each is hidden by the table gate:
1. **U+00A0.** All four Thabit styles gain U+00A0, from a glyph that exists only in the 2010 save. land.py's exact-codepoint check refuses it. A documented dropglyph edit fixes it (verified).
2. **The obliques are not italic.** Both lose the ITALIC style bit and are named like the uprights, because build.py's naming step and FontForge's name-derived italic are not reproduced.
3. **USE_TYPO_METRICS.** The converter sets it for OS/2 v1 releases where FontForge did not. That changes line spacing, markedly for Lohit-Tamil, which the agent calls landable and 0/0.
4. **The Bengali marker already exists.** The 'cheaper partial fix' for Lohit-Bengali is already in babelfont, but mis-cased ('# Automatic code start'). Fixing the string is the first upstream step and reproduces the agent's 284 -> 117 words.

Other revisions:
- The spacing-combining PR must also change SetSubcategory, which the recipe always runs.
- implied-oncurves models only one of FontForge's two numbering paths.
- The copyright edit does not reproduce the release string.
- mergepsfont's worth-outputting test is not FontForge's.

Nothing new is landable. At best, Lohit-Bengali and Lohit-Tamil are table-clean after re-pairing, and neither is functionally equivalent yet. Thabit needs the uni00A0 drop, the oblique naming and italic work, and the Latin SplineSetsTTFApprox port (or a decision) on top of everything the agent listed.

rows.row: BUILD-FAILED: operation 'Fontc' ... FEA parsing failed with 2 errors
rows.cause: Cardo-Regular-TTF.sfd names a glyph `10192.04` (gid 3416, Encoding 62520 = U+F438, a salt alternate listed in the AlternateSubs2 of u10192 and u10198). FontForge never goes through FEA, so it exported it (the release post table still names U+F438 `10192.04`). babelfont writes the lookups as FEA, and the OpenType Feature File spec (2.f.i) says a glyph name must not start with a digit. fea-rs rejects both references: 'Unexpected token, expected glyph or glyph class' at `sub u10192 from [Sigma Sigma.09 u10192.03 10192.04];` and `sub u10198 from [u10198.01 10192.04 ...];`. This is not a fontc bug: fontTools feaLib rejects the same FEA. It is a source name that FEA cannot express. Closed by the documented .sfd rename below. The new name is a choice, not a fidelity value, which is why this row is classed as a decision.
rows.evidence: Full diagnostic from fontc (fontc-worktrees/survey-rebase debug build; gftools-builder3 e851b8b with fontc 1.0.0 shows only the count). Minimal repro: investigations/next-cardo/probes/fea_digit_glyphname/{make.py,run.sh,EXPECTED.txt}. DigitName fails in fontc 1.0.0 (builder3 e851b8b) and in feaLib ('Expected glyph name ... found 10192.04'); LetterName (u10192.04) builds in both. After the rename (runs/r1-regular-rename) the style builds and the shared gate shows 1 row.

rows.cause: FontForge tottf.c, unchanged from tag v20110222 to 20170731, sets dirhint = 0 when the exported glyphs include both left-to-right and right-to-left characters (-2 when only RTL, else 2) and sets head.flags bit 9 when it sees RTL. Commit 722e7ea8873e (2017-12-23, 'Skip Apple head table fields in OpenType mode', first in release 20190317) makes OpenType mode write 2 unconditionally. The release was exported by FontForge build 2011-02-22 (FFTM stamp) and Cardo maps Hebrew plus Latin, so it gets 0. fontc 1.0.0 always writes 2: write-fonts Head::default has font_direction_hint 2, fontbe head.rs never overrides it, and FEA can set only FontRevision in the head table (fea-rs HeadBuilder). No Glyphs or FEA source can express the value. The OpenType spec deprecates the field ('Set to 2'), and neither harfrust 0.6.2 nor skrifa 0.47.0 reads it. The row is functionally empty.
rows.evidence: FontForge sources fetched for tags v20110222, v20120731-b, 20141230, 20150824, 20161012, 20170731, 20190317, 20190413, 20190801 and 20230101; the commit list for tottf.c between 2017-07-31 and 2019-08 names 722e7ea8873e. probes/dirhint_oracle.py (runs/dirhint_oracle.txt) computes the pre-722e7ea rule from each release's cmap and matches 147 of 149 releases in both batches. The 2 misses are Tuffy-Regular and Tuffy-Italic, which have no FFTM table and ship 2. All 3 Cardo styles and both Thabit styles have 0, MATCH, bit9=1, FFTM 2011-02-22 or 2008-08-08. probes/table_gate_proposed.py reclassifies this row as RELEASE-STALE in Cardo x3 and Thabit x2 (runs/dirhint_thabit_proposed.txt).

rows.row: hmtx.uni0304 {width:[1000,0]} and hmtx.uni05B105BD {width:[1300,0]} (hidden by the shared gate)
rows.cause: Both glyphs are GlyphClass 4 (mark) with an attach anchor and a non-zero advance (Width 1000 and 1300), and FontForge exported those advances. babelfont's SFD reader gives every GlyphClass-4 glyph subCategory Nonspacing, and --set-subcategory sets Nonspacing again on any mark with an _anchor. glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 then exports a Nonspacing mark at zero width (source.rs:1828). The shared gate never reported the difference: diffenator3 replaced the hmtx section with 'There are 240 changes, check manually!', and table_gate.expand_overflow recomputes only left side bearings.
rows.evidence: probes/advance_audit.py (runs/advance_audit_cardo_r0r1.txt): uni0304 1000 vs 0 and uni05B105BD 1300 vs 0 are HIDDEN in r1. The prototype (reader plus set-subcategory emit 'Spacing Combining' for an advancing mark) gives 0 advance differences in runs/p2-proto/advance_audit.txt, and the proposed gate goes from 2 rows to 0.

rows.row: GPOS mark attachment lost; the gate waved it through as 'legacy kern modernised' (not a blocking row)
rows.cause: babelfont's FontForge reader (upstream commit 66334a7) starts the abvm/blwm/kern/dist/mark/mkmk feature blocks it writes with '# Automatic code start'. fea-rs has_insert_marker and ufo2ft match only '# Automatic Code', case-sensitively. fontc therefore treats the mark feature as hand-written and skips its mark writer: 'Skipping generating feature mark, which is manually declared in FEA and has no insertion comment'. No MarkBasePos lookup is built from the 12 Anchor-N classes. kern is not affected: glyphs-reader appends '# Automatic Code' to any manual kern feature.
rows.evidence: fontc warning reproduced with builder3 e851b8b. probes/shaping_compare.py on runs/r1-regular-rename: 4361 of 181328 base+mark strings and all 45 diffenator3 Hebrew words differ. With the prototype marker fix (runs/p1-proto) 956 base+mark strings and 7 words still differ. probes/automatic_code_marker.py (runs/automatic_code_marker.txt): only Cardo-Regular (mark) and Lohit-Bengali (abvm) lose a writer in the next batch, and no landed repository does.

rows.row: GPOS: marks attached to glyphs made of references (not a gate row)
rows.cause: fontc propagates anchors from components as Glyphs.app does. FontForge exports only a glyph's own anchors, so 1680 reference-only glyphs such as igrave became bases the release never had. The next-provenance unit's filter --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation (Glyphs 'Propagate Anchors' = 0) removes this.
rows.evidence: Stage p1 (marker fix only) vs p2 (plus --fontforge-no-anchor-propagation): base+mark differences go from 956 to 10 of 181328 (runs/shaping_summary.txt). Example in p1: U+00EC U+0300, where the release leaves the mark unattached and ours attaches it.

rows.row: GPOS lookup order: 10 base+mark strings and 7 diffenator3 words, Hebrew cantillation over vowel points (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release applies FontForge's lookups in .sfd order, which interleaves the mark-to-base lookups (0,1,2,5,6,7,9,10,14,21) with the pair and contextual lookups of the same mark feature. fea-rs inserts generated lookups at next_gpos_id() at the marker (compile_ctx.rs). babelfont defines every FontForge lookup in featurePrefixes, so all 12 generated MarkBasePos lookups come after them (our lookups 20-31).
rows.evidence: probes/lookup_order_test.py: reordering the RELEASE's GPOS the way fontc orders ours makes it equal to our build on all 17 strings. Putting its MarkBasePos lookups FIRST instead leaves the release unchanged on all 241128 base+mark strings and the 17 strings (runs/p2-proto/Cardo-Regular.lookup-order-test*.txt). probes/mark_lookups_after_marker.py moves the 12 lookups that the kern and mark features own after their marker in the .glyphs, and a real builder3 e851b8b build of that file gives 0/181328 base+mark, 0/41683 pairs, 0/15 kern+mark and 0 d3 words, with proposed gate 0 (runs/p3-marks-first).

rows.cause: The .sfd states nonbreakingspace Width 550 and space Width 575. google/fonts d70318ab8 (Dave Crossland, 2015-04-27, 'Updating ofl/cardo/*ttf with nbspace and fsType fixes') edited only Cardo-Italic.ttf. In that binary it changed only the nonbreakingspace advance, 550 to 575 (the space's), plus the cmap re-packing (mappings equal) and the head checksum. fsType was already 0 before and after.
rows.evidence: probes/cardo_release_history.py (runs/cardo_release_history.txt): 90abd17b4 to d70318ab8 changes tables [cmap, head, hmtx], advances [(nonbreakingspace, 550, 575)], cmap mappings equal: True. Regular and Bold binaries are unchanged since 90abd17b4. Edit `nbspwidth` verified in runs/s1-italic-nbsp: the row closes and 10 shared rows become 6.

rows.cause: Only the lookup order differs: babelfont defines 'Single Substitution lookup 9' (longs->s, in no feature and called only by the hist contextual lookup) before the chain that calls it, so every later index shifts by one. Feature membership and rules are equal. arbitrate_gsub_lookup_order refused only because its shaping corpus met the nbsp advance difference ('  ': release 575, ours 550).
rows.evidence: GATE_TRACE=1 on r0: 'shaping differs lang=None word=\' \\xa0\''. After the nbspwidth edit (runs/s1-italic-nbsp) the gate prints 'RELEASE-STALE the same GSUB lookups in a different order; 69696 shaped runs identical across 8 language(s), with the features firing'.

rows.row: hmtx.uni1DC1 [30,0], hmtx.uni2E0F [2443,0], hmtx.uni2E10 [2443,0], hmtx.uni05B105BD [1300,0], plus hidden hmtx.uni2E11 [2443,0] and hmtx.uniF15B [11,0]
rows.cause: All 6 are GlyphClass 4 with a non-zero Width, and the release keeps both GDEF class 3 and the advance. The babelfont SFD reader writes subCategory Nonspacing, and fontc zeroes a Nonspacing mark. uni2E11 and uniF15B were hidden by table_gate.arbitrate_lsb: it marks a whole hmtx row RELEASE-STALE when the release's bearing is stale, even when the row also carries a width difference. Its '"advance" not in row' guard looks for a key diffenator3 never writes; the key is 'width'.
rows.evidence: probes/advance_audit.py lists them as HIDDEN (lsb-arbitration). With the prototype (runs/p2-proto) there are 0 advance differences, and the 6 glyphs are width 30/2443/2443/2443/11/1300 with GDEF class 3 in both fonts.

rows.cause: The .sfd states 15 LCarets2 records (with LigCaretCntFixed: 1), and FontForge's GDEF writer exported them (tottfgpos.c LigCaretCnt/DumpLigCarets: non-zero carets, or all carets when the count is fixed; ascending, descending for RTL). babelfont stores LCarets2 as format_specific 'sfd.lcarets' and never turns it into Glyphs caret_N anchors, which fontbe get_ligature_carets would compile.
rows.evidence: The prototype adds caret_N anchors: 15 LigGlyphs, equal to the release (runs/p2-proto). probes/lcarets_census.py: Cardo-Italic is the only style in either batch with exportable carets, and its release has 15.

rows.cause: Same as Cardo-Regular: FontForge 2011-02-22 wrote 0 for a font with both LTR and RTL characters. fontc writes 2. The field is deprecated.
rows.evidence: runs/dirhint_oracle.txt: Cardo-Italic 0 0 MATCH bit9=1. The proposed gate reclassifies it (runs/p2-proto/Cardo-Italic.proposed.txt).

rows.row: GDEF.mark_glyph_sets [null, {0:[uni1DC1 ... uni05B105BD]}] and 'GDEF.glyph_classes -- a lookup filters on glyph class' (appear once advancing marks keep their width)
rows.cause: The release's kern lookup has flag 0, from the .sfd `Lookup: 258 0 0`. fontc's kern writer (ufo2ft KernFeatureWriter semantics) always ignores marks. When some marks advance, it uses UseMarkFilteringSet over those marks, which adds the MarkGlyphSetsDef and a class-reading flag. fontir 1.0.0 feature_writers.rs:197-200 turns ufo2ft's ignoreMarks=false into a hard error, although fontbe kern.rs:1130 already has the ignore_marks=false path. The same gap exists at r0 (kern flag 8 vs 0), where the gate hid it.
rows.evidence: runs/p2-proto: shared 3 rows, proposed 2. probes/simulate_kern_flag0.py clears bits 0x8/0x10 and the filtering set on the kern-writer lookups of the p2 build, then re-runs d3 and both gates: shared 1, proposed 0 (runs/p2-sim-kernflag0). This is a SIMULATION, not a build.

rows.row: kern across a combining mark: 2056 of 3057 kerned pairs with U+0301/U+0308/U+0323 between (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release's flag-0 kern lookup lets an intervening mark block the pair; our IgnoreMarks lookup kerns across it. The gate accepts any GPOS difference when both fonts have lookups.
rows.evidence: probes/shaping_compare.py corpus kern+mark: r0, s1 and p2 all show 2056/3057; the p2 build with simulated flag-0 kern shows 0/3057 (runs/shaping_summary.txt).

rows.cause: Same rule: FontForge 2011-02-22, the release maps Hebrew and Latin, so 0. fontc writes 2. The field is deprecated.
rows.evidence: runs/dirhint_oracle.txt Cardo-Bold 0 0 MATCH bit9=1. runs/s1-bold-workarounds: shared 1 row, proposed 0.

rows.cause: fontc 1.0.0 ignores a single-master Glyphs source's instance weightClass (issues/fontc-static-weight-class.md). The .sfd states TTFWeight: 700. tools/land.py closes it inside the convert commit with tools/workarounds.py (weight-class as FEA). baseline.sh measures the converter alone, so the row always appears there. The unit brief said Bold had only head.font_direction_hint; baseline-next.tsv shows both rows.
rows.evidence: Run through next-fstype/probes/bf_with_workarounds.sh (WORKAROUNDS=1 in probes/run_stage.sh), runs/s1-bold-workarounds goes from 2 shared rows to 1.

rows.row: kern across a combining mark: 177 of 426 kerned pairs (not a gate row)
rows.cause: The release kern lookup has flag 0, and the release also classes U+0300.. as base (the gate discloses the 163 GDEF mark classes as a correction). Our kern writer lookups have IgnoreMarks, so 'B + U+0301 + A' kerns in ours (B 1379) and not in the release (B 1482).

proposed_sfd_edits.commit_subject: Rename glyph 10192.04 to u10192.04 in Cardo-Regular-TTF.sfd
proposed_sfd_edits.commit_body:
A feature file cannot name a glyph that starts with a digit (OpenType
Feature File spec 2.f.i), so the salt rules of u10192 and u10198 that
list it could not be compiled. The new name follows the glyph's
siblings u10192.03 and u10198.01-.05. Only the post name of U+F438
changes; outline, advance and mappings are unchanged.
proposed_sfd_edits.value_derived_from: The source's own naming of the other salt alternates of U+10192 and U+10198 (u10192.03, u10198.01, u10198.03-.05). The release keeps the name 10192.04, because FontForge wrote the .sfd name into post format 2. The gate reports the rename as ACCEPTED-RENAME cmap U+F438 (same outline and advance).
proposed_sfd_edits.source_currently_states: StartChar: 10192.04 / Encoding: 62520 62520 3416 / Width: 1088 / GlyphClass: 2, referenced in two AlternateSubs2 lines of "'salt' Stylistic Alternatives in Latin lookup 24 subtable" (glyphs u10192 and u10198)

proposed_sfd_edits.commit_subject: Give nonbreakingspace the space's width in Cardo-Italic-TTF.sfd

proposed_tool_changes.description: An advancing mark is 'Spacing Combining', not 'Nonspacing'. The SFD reader (GlyphClass 4 with a non-zero Width) and the --set-subcategory filter (a mark with an _anchor and a non-zero advance in any layer) both set it. A Glyphs compiler exports a Nonspacing mark zero-width (glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 source.rs:1828); a SpacingCombining mark keeps its advance and stays GDEF class 3. The reader half is the next-provenance unit's babelfont-spacing-combining-mark.patch; the set-subcategory half is new here, because that filter overwrote the reader's value for marks with anchors (Cardo-Regular uni0304 and uni05B105BD).
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Italic: 6 hmtx rows close (2 of them hidden by the gate). Regular: 2 hidden rows close. Lohit-Tamil u0BC1 and u0BC2 close (runs/reg-proto: 8 -> 6 rows). 0 advance differences in all three Cardo p2 builds. Side effect: fontc's kern writer then uses a mark filtering set over these marks (Italic GDEF.mark_glyph_sets row); see the fontc change below.
proposed_tool_changes.prototype: same patch: convertors/fontforge.rs glyph finalization and filters/setsubcategory.rs

proposed_tool_changes.description: Keep FontForge's lookup precedence around compiler-generated lookups. For a feature that carries the insertion marker, define the lookups that only this feature references after the marker, inside the feature block, rather than in featurePrefixes. fea-rs then inserts the generated mark-to-base lookups before them (InsertionPoint = next_gpos_id() at the marker) instead of after every lookup the file defines. A lookup used by another feature or by a contextual lookup stays in the prefix.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: Cardo-Regular with every other fix still differs in 10 base+mark strings and 7 diffenator3 words (Hebrew cantillation over vowels). probes/lookup_order_test.py shows the order is the whole cause, and that the release's MarkBasePos lookups placed first shape identically to the release (0/241128). probes/mark_lookups_after_marker.py applies this layout to the converted .glyphs, and a real builder3 e851b8b / fontc 1.0.0 build of it gives 0 differences in every corpus and proposed gate 0 (runs/p3-marks-first). This is EMULATED on the .glyphs, not implemented in Rust. The general case (FontForge interleaving that marks-first does not reproduce) would need explicit FEA mark lookups in .sfd order.
proposed_tool_changes.upstream_pr_needed: babelfont-rs (simoncozens): design change to discuss with Simon before a PR.

proposed_tool_changes.description: Honour ufo2ft's KernFeatureWriter option ignoreMarks=false (featureWriters userData) instead of rejecting it as unsupported. fontbe already has the path (KernSplitOptions.ignore_marks / make_lookups). Companion babelfont change: when a FontForge source's kern lookups carry no IgnoreMarks flag, write that featureWriters option into the Glyphs userData, so the kern lookup keeps FontForge's flag 0 and gets no spacing-mark filtering set.
proposed_tool_changes.evidence: fontir 1.0.0 feature_writers.rs:197-200 hard-errors on 'KernFeatureWriter ignoreMarks=false'; fontbe kern.rs:1130 has the branch. decisions_for_felipe: Where to land Cardo. googlefonts/CardoFont is ARCHIVED on GitHub (read-only; archived: true, last push 2021-03-01, 2 forks, open issue #1 from 2017 'Glyph differences amongst Italic and Roman' that its author chose to ignore). Its main (fc675d7, identical on GitHub and in the repo archive) is 3 commits past the recorded b2bf876, all by Marc Foley on 2017-06-09: 'converd .sfd to .glyphs', 'updated metadata to match gf spec', 'fonts now compile'. They add an unshipped Glyphs 2 conversion (appVersion 1032): sources/Cardo.glyphs with 2 masters (Regular + Bold, version 1.500, 3844 glyphs, 10192.04 dropped, 576 glyphs lacking a layer) and sources/Cardo-Italic.glyphs (2388 glyphs). There is no config.yaml and no fonts, and nothing was built or shipped from them. land.py (kind upstream) would branch modernize-sfd-to-glyphs from b2bf876, diverging from main. A googlefonts admin must unarchive the repository before any push; otherwise use another repository. You also decide what happens to Marc's .glyphs on main.
The new name for glyph 10192.04 (proposed u10192.04, after its siblings). Only U+F438's post name changes.

Adopt the gate changes: advance widths can no longer be hidden, and head.font_direction_hint is arbitrated for pre-2019 FontForge exports. Decide whether a .notdef advance counts: the change newly blocks landed Kristi-Regular and NosiferCaps-Regular (.notdef 748 vs 1024). Tuffy's plan already made an .notdef edit.

Replace the gate's structural GPOS acceptance with a shaping test. That would reopen landed repositories the current gate passed: Italiana-Regular kerns 726 of 13689 letter pairs twice (-40 against -20), and Salsa-Regular kerns across marks in 246 of 285 cases. Ultra-Regular (260 pairs) needs its own unit.

Kern lookup mark flags, which is family-independent: file fontc ignoreMarks=false parity (plus a babelfont userData entry), or accept and disclose kern-across-mark differences (Cardo-Bold 177/426, Cardo-Italic 2056/3057). Cardo-Italic cannot be CLEAN under either gate without that fontc change once its advancing marks keep their widths. The alternative is zeroed advances (6 hmtx rows).

Which route to pitch to Simon for FontForge lookup precedence: FEA lookups defined after the feature's marker (verified for Cardo by emulation), or explicit FEA mark lookups in .sfd order (general, but duplicates the anchor data).

The cause is glyf header bounding boxes, not outlines. Bold: all within 2 units. edit_verdicts.commit_subject: Set the vertical metrics the 2012 release carries
edit_verdicts.reason: The values reproduce independently: 1864/629/-629 = int() of the true extremes, both of the .sfd outlines and of the release's own TTF outlines (which vmetcheck.py measures). FontForge's own rule gives 1881/631/1881/-632, and no rule gives 629 from the stated offset 3 (on-curve 631, all-points 639, #85 633). The value's origin is disclosed. The absolute form (flag 0 + value) is the same shape as tools/bbox/vmetcorrect.py's set_os2_vert, so it is the natural .sfd form, and it is converter-rule independent (CLEAN in runs/01 and with the filter in runs/04). Typo descender -634 is correctly left alone. Optional wording fixes: (a) 'head.modified says 2012-08-20' is not evidence of the METRICS edit by itself, because the same hg commit added ttfautohint hinting, which re-stamps modified. The stronger evidence is the 21 all-point glyph boxes plus 9 hmtx LSBs that kept FontForge's on-curve value while glyf xMin moved to the all-point minimum (runs/limelight_hmtx_vs_glyf.txt). (b) Say 'the int() rule of tools/bbox/vmetcheck.py and vmetcorrect.py', not that the script was run: neither script's automated output matches the release, since both would also change TypoDescent.

tool_verdicts.reason: The code matches FontForge b69c9652/c9ca2f32 (dumpglyph and dumpcomposite on-curve QuickBounds with floor/ceil, sethhead truncation and widening, WinBB). The SFD reader keeps flag-128 implied points as QCurve nodes, so they count as on-curve, as FontForge's SplinePoints do. My rebuild from the diff reproduces every harness result, and on all 149 styles it equals an independent model on 328/328 metrics and moves nothing else. Tests and fmt pass. Mergeability: it is opt-in; there is precedent for filters reading sfd.* keys (fontforgeos2defaults reads sfd.width_set); no sfd.* keys leak into .glyphs output; it depends only on the open #91-#93 for its group line. Requested revisions to the doc comment/PR text, none blocking: (1) state that the pre-2014-10 sethhead quirk (hhea descender's mode taken from HheadAOffset) is not modelled. (2) Do not claim the rule is universal for pre-2014 FontForge: GiveYouGlory is a clean 20110222 export (head created == modified, 339 FontForge on-curve boxes, 0 all-point) where it misses 2 of 4 metrics (runs/indep_bounds_pr85_pairs.txt, runs/glyph_boxes_giveyouglory.txt, runs/stamps.txt). (3) 'Must run first' is design rationale only: with the flag last, MoC-Bold and NYCD give identical results (runs/07-flag-last).

tool_verdicts.tool_change: sfd-reland tools/recipe.py: insert --fontforge-legacy-offset-metrics first when the release's FFTM build stamp < 1410896146 (ee15007274e9)
tool_verdicts.reason: The cutoff is the verified commit time of ee15007274e9. It uses the same FFTM mechanism as --fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean. It adds the flag to all 141 FFTM-stamped styles, but only 4 change (runs/impl_vs_model.txt), and none moves away from its release. The FFTM stamp is FontForge's library_source_modtime (ttfspecial.c ttf_fftm_dump), so a stamp can only postdate the code, never predate it; the gate cannot wrongly apply the pre-2014 rule to post-2014 code. Apply only after the converter change is merged upstream and the pinned converter is rebuilt from a published revision, as the investigation says.

classification_objections: MountainsofChristmas-Bold OS/2.us_weight_class [700, 400] is labelled 'compiler-gap'. That label is not in the taxonomy the workflow journal uses. Every earlier unit classified the identical fontc single-master weightClass row as 'converter-fidelity': corben-bold, heights (NosiferCaps, UnifrakturCook-Bold), nosifer, puritan (Bold, BoldItalic), small (ComicRelief-Bold), tuffy, play (Play-Bold). Relabel it converter-fidelity. It is closed by tools/workarounds.py weight_class, which I reproduced: runs/03 has 0 blocking rows. The other 10 rows' classifications are correct: Limelight 5 x source-edit-from-release; MoC-Bold 3 and NYCD 2 x converter-fidelity.
missed: googlefontdirectory-hg 927784141:tools/bbox/ also holds vmetcorrect.py, which APPLIES the same int() rule the result cites from vmetcheck.py. It sets each metric's IsOffset to 0 and writes the absolute value (set_os2_vert), exactly the shape of the proposed .sfd edit, then calls FontForge Generate. It cannot be the final writer: it would also set TypoDescent -629, its WinDescent branch writes the negative ymin, and a FontForge Generate would give created == modified and on-curve boxes. It should still be named as the repository's tool for this rule.

Extra evidence for the Limelight post-export rewrite that the result did not use (runs/limelight_hmtx_vs_glyf.txt). All 9 RELEASE-STALE hmtx rows in the gate have the same fingerprint: hmtx lsb is FontForge's on-curve x-minimum while glyf xMin is the all-point minimum (e.g. 'one' lsb 1 vs xMin -2; 'seven' 64 vs 61). The boxes were therefore recomputed without touching hmtx, which is what a fontTools/ttx compile (recalcBBoxes) does. FontForge writes lsb and xMin from the same box, and ttfautohint keeps glyf headers. This narrows the 'tool not identified' item, though it does not prove it.

GiveYouGlory is mischaracterised. The result says its 621 'suggests another post-export edit', but by the result's own discriminators it is a clean FontForge 20110222 export: head.created == head.modified (2011-07-08 07:31:04); FFTM sourceModified == the .sfd ModificationTime (1310121007); 339 glyph boxes are FontForge on-curve boxes and 0 are all-point (runs/stamps.txt, runs/glyph_boxes_giveyouglory.txt). Yet the pre-2014 rule gives 619/-624 against the release's 621/-625, and vmetcheck's rule gives -621 against -625, so it is not a vmetcheck edit either. Neither rule explains it; the stated offsets at export may have differed. At b69c9652, sf->modificationtime is bumped only by Font Info OK (fontinfo.c GFI_OK -> SFSetModTime), not by saving, outline edits or scripted SetOS2Value, so FFTM == ModificationTime does not prove the exported metrics equal the committed file. It is outside both tables, so no row here changes, but it lowers confidence that the filter's rule is complete.

Minor evidence caveats. The control counts '137/143' cover simple glyphs only, and MoC-Bold's control is v1.002 (90abd17b4), not the paired v1.003 release. Counting composites, the paired releases have 193 and 295 FontForge-box glyphs and 0 all-point-only; the conclusion is unchanged. The '10 s after the save' wording is loose: FFTM sourceModified is the last Font Info OK time (sf->modificationtime), not the save time. The extreme-setting glyph names have ties: Rcommaaccent/kcommaaccent for the Limelight minimum, Hcircumflex/Ecircumflex for the NYCD maximum.

No pairing mistakes were found. families-next.tsv has no duplicate style rows. Limelight's two candidates are resolved correctly (FFTM sourceModified = -TTF.sfd, not -OTF.sfd). NYCD's and Limelight's shipped blobs are the hg files. MoC-Bold's 2017 hotfix did not touch vertical metrics or outlines.
result.overall:
The investigation holds. Using my own parser, the FontForge source I fetched myself, harness runs and a rebuild of the prototype from its diff, I reproduced:
- every row cause and every harness result;
- the 305/298/295 model counts;
- the "4 styles change, none regresses" claim.

The Rust filter matches an independent model on all 328 offset-mode metrics in both tables. The Limelight .sfd edit is sound: its values equal int() of both the source's and the release's true extremes. The edit closes all 5 rows.

Weak points, none of which change a row or block landing:
1. The us_weight_class row uses a new label, 'compiler-gap'. Every earlier unit called the same row converter-fidelity.
2. vmetcorrect.py is omitted. It is the repository's tool that applies the cited rule, in the same IsOffset=0 + value shape as the proposed edit.
3. GiveYouGlory is mischaracterised. By the result's own tests it is a clean FontForge 20110222 export, yet the filter's rule misses 2 of its 4 metrics. The upstream PR should present the rule as validated on the 82 offset-mode styles of these tables, not as complete for pre-2014 FontForge.
4. The Limelight commit body leans on head.modified, which ttfautohint alone explains. The hmtx-vs-glyf fingerprint is better evidence.

Families landable after the changes, as the result says:
- limelight: the edit alone.
- nothingyoucoulddo: the babelfont filter plus the recipe change.
- mountainsofchristmas: the filter, the recipe change and land.py's existing weight-class workaround.

All three still wait on #91-#93 and the new PR being merged upstream.
