tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs: write the insertion marker as '# Automatic Code' instead of '# Automatic code start'
tool_verdicts.reason:
Confirmed in code. fontforge.rs:3759 (integration 17ea899, introduced by upstream 66334a7) writes '# Automatic code start'. fea-rs 1.0.0 token_tree/typed.rs statements() keeps only comments that start with '# Automatic Code', and fontbe features.rs:803-812 then drops the writer for that tag. glyphs-reader re-adds the marker only for kern.

The r1 build has no MarkBasePos lookup at all, and the gate still passed its GPOS. My p1 build: base+mark 4361 -> 956. babelfont's own subsetlayout.rs:871 already tests '# Automatic Code'. It is a one-line fix an upstream maintainer can merge.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs: LCarets2 -> caret_N anchors (plus LigCaretCntFixed)
tool_verdicts.reason:
The rule matches FontForge v20110222 tottfgpos.c LigCaretCnt/DumpLigCarets: non-zero carets unless the count is fixed; ascending, descending when SCRightToLeft. fontbe marks.rs get_ligature_carets compiles caret anchors without needing a category.

My p2 Italic build has LigCaretList 15, equal to the .sfd and the release (e.g. f_f_i [1117, 2057]).

Minor: the prototype approximates SCRightToLeft by codepoint ranges. FontForge infers the script of an unencoded glyph (SCScriptFromUnicode), so an unencoded RTL ligature would be sorted the wrong way. No Cardo glyph is affected.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs: an advancing GlyphClass-4 mark is 'Spacing Combining' (reader + --set-subcategory)
tool_verdicts.reason:
Confirmed.
- The reader maps GlyphClass 4 to Mark with subCategory Nonspacing (fontforge.rs:1583-1605).
- setsubcategory.rs sets Nonspacing on any mark with an _anchor.
- glyphs2fontir 1.0.0 source.rs:1828 zeroes a Nonspacing mark.

After the change, my p2 builds have 0 advance differences (Regular 3845, Italic 2387). Functional effect: HarfBuzz already zeroes GDEF marks when it shapes, so the gain is the hmtx table and consumers that read hmtx directly.

The unit is right that on Italic this change creates the MarkGlyphSetsDef/UseMarkFilteringSet row, so it must land together with the kern-flag fix (below).

tool_verdicts.tool_change: babelfont-rs: define a marker-carrying feature's own lookups after the marker (lookup placement)
tool_verdicts.reason:
Reproduced independently. Their emulation, applied to MY p2 .glyphs and built with builder3 e851b8b, gives shared 1 / proposed 0 and 0 differences in base+mark, pairs and kern+mark. My multi-mark corpus also gives 0 (heb3 13392, heb4 12555, hebsh 868, lat3 28704, grk3 5390). At p2 there are 488+630 stacked Hebrew differences, so the evidence is stronger than the 10 strings and 7 words reported.

It is still an emulation on .glyphs text, and 'marks-first' is not the release's actual interleaving. It is right to present it as a design question for Simon.

tool_verdicts.tool_change: fontc: honour KernFeatureWriter ignoreMarks=false (+ babelfont userData entry)
tool_verdicts.reason:
The fontc gap is real and a PR is plausible: fontir 1.0.0 feature_writers.rs:197-200 hard-errors, and fontbe KernSplitOptions.ignore_marks already exists. The simulation reproduces: Italic kern+mark 2056/3057 -> 0.

The styles_affected list and the need are overstated, in two places:

(1) Cardo-Bold does not need it. Its release (FontForge gdefclass: no GlyphClass, no anchors) classes all 2992 glyphs as base, while ours classes 165 combining marks as marks.
- Simulation: giving our p2 Bold the release's GDEF classes and leaving IgnoreMarks in place closes kern+mark 177/426 -> 0 (runs/sim_bold_release_gdef.txt).
- Real build: stating FontForge's GlyphClassDef as an FEA 'table GDEF' prefix (probes/emulate_ff_gdef_fea.py, builder3 e851b8b / fontc 1.0.0) gives GDEF {1:2992} equal to the release, kern+mark 0/426 and proposed gate 0 (runs/emu-bold-ffgdef-fea). No fontc change is involved.
- A Glyphs 'category = Letter' route does NOT work: fontc then emits no GDEF, HarfBuzz synthesizes classes from Unicode, kern+mark stays 177 and base+mark rises 744 -> 4844 (runs/emu-bold-ffgdef).

(2) Salsa-Regular (landed cb27c62) is mis-attributed. Our landed build has NO GDEF, and the release classes gravecomb/acutecomb (advance 334) as base.
- Clearing the kern flags leaves kern+mark at 246/285 and base+mark at 257/282, because HarfBuzz still zero-widths U+0300/U+0301.
- Copying the release GDEF closes both: 0/285 and 0/282 (runs/salsa_landed_causes.txt).

The fontc change is needed for Cardo-Italic, whose release classes U+0301 etc. as marks with a flag-0 kern; runs/emu-italic-ffgdef-fea shows the FEA GDEF leaves Italic at 2056. Poly/Varela were not checked and should be re-derived the same way.

tool_verdicts.reason: glyphs-reader 1.0.0 font.rs:1164 honours 'Propagate Anchors'. p1 -> p2 (the only change is the flag) reproduced: base+mark 956 -> 10. My multi-mark lat3 corpus goes 261 -> 0. The claim is FontForge exporting only a glyph's own anchors, consistent with tottfgpos.c. This is owned by the next-provenance proposal.

tool_verdicts.reason:
(a) Both bugs are confirmed in 2f43693.

The unifraktur precedent called that correction inert, but it is not inert in Cardo-Bold (kern) or in landed Salsa (base+mark 257/282: combining grave/acute lose their 334 advance).

tool_verdicts.reason:
Reproduced: feaLib rejects '10192.04' at the glyph position. builder3 prints only 'FEA parsing failed with N errors'; the fontc CLI (survey-rebase debug) prints the location.

Extend the babelfont check beyond a leading digit to any name outside the FEA glyph-name alphabet. Cardo-Italic has '1E0A' and 'uniA78#' (U+A783). Neither is referenced by the converted FEA today, but any FEA that lists them fails: my FEA-GDEF emulation hit 'Invalid char '#' in glyph name'.

Two causes co-exist: fontc's IgnoreMarks flag, and the GDEF classes. babelfont leaves the 165 zero-width combining marks uncategorised and fontc's GlyphData makes them marks, whereas FontForge 20110222 gdefclass() exported every glyph as base. The shaping corpus's base+mark+mark set is EMPTY for all three styles. 'Hebrew' counts presentation forms, so it exceeds the 40-base cap, and no stacked cluster was ever shaped. My probes/multimark_compare.py (60909 strings) confirms p3 Regular = 0. It shows lookup order causes 1118 stacked differences at p2, not only 10 strings. It adds 1303 (Bold, all <=1 unit) and 1542 (Italic, 341 over 10 units, worst 13) stacked fallback-positioning differences to the unresolved fallback item (runs/p2/multimark_deltas.txt).

Our build has no GDEF, so HarfBuzz zero-widths gravecomb/acutecomb (hmtx 334, class base in the release). This is a pre-existing landed-repo problem, found while checking the unit's Salsa claim.

Cardo-Italic GDEF ligature class: the release classes 18 glyphs as ligatures. p2 gets 15 of them (the ones with carets); A_R and uniFB4F (.sfd GlyphClass: 3) and f_j (Ligature2) stay unclassed. The gate's GDEF arbitration discusses only marks. This is inert today: no MarkLigPos and no IgnoreLigatures lookup.

Cardo-Italic glyph names that FEA cannot express, '1E0A' and 'uniA78#' (U+A783). They are harmless now, but they block any FEA-based fix that lists them (including the GDEF route) and should be in the diagnostics proposal.
Minor inconsistency in the unit's own numbers: unresolved says Bold 746 / Italic 840 base+mark fallback strings, while shaping_summary and rows_after say 744 / 839. My runs give 744 / 839.

The fallback-offset cause could be stated more precisely. The release's composite glyf headers match none of control box, on-curve box or outline for 81 (Italic), 192 (Bold) and 286 (Regular) composites (probes/composite_bbox_rule.py). Example: Italic uni0312 header yMin 1170 vs outline 1158 vs control box 1133; ours writes the control box, as fontTools does. HarfBuzz fallback reads these headers. FreeType places the outline from the points (probes/stale_lsb_render.py), so the stale bearings do not move rendered glyphs.

The exclude_dflt and aalt prototype, rebuilt by me from the published diff, makes all 12 language systems equal (Poly-Italic 2 and Varela 10) structurally and under HarfBuzz.

- The aalt heuristic's warn-only gap already occurs in Play-Regular.
- The diff needs rebasing before an upstream PR, and exclude_dflt should be filed separately from the aalt heuristic.
